event.title: Message containing personal data
event.description: The citizen includes identifiers in the question. Deterministic masking replaces each item with a token before any processing; only types and counts are traced.

responses.message:
As a precaution, I masked the personal data in your message (numbers, email addresses): it is neither stored nor transmitted. Please avoid sharing it here.

The law limits the normal working time to **forty hours per week** for all workers in non‑agricultural public or private establishments[1].  

**Explanation**  
- This ceiling applies regardless of the employee’s age, sex or type of pay.  
- Only a decree, after consulting the national labour commission, may allow exceptions and must specify the conditions and the extra‑pay for overtime[1].  

**What you can do**  
1. Check whether your contract or a collective agreement contains a specific clause that authorises overtime; such a clause must be based on a valid decree.  
2. If you are asked to work beyond 40 hours and no decree applies, you may:  
   - Discuss the matter with your employer and request that the extra hours respect the legal limits and the required overtime premium.  
   - Contact the **Ministry of Labour** or the **National Labour Commission** to verify whether a decree authorising the extra hours exists.  
   - If the employer persists, you can file a complaint with the **Labour Inspectorate** (Inspection du travail) for a violation of the Code du travail.  

These steps will help you ensure that your working time respects the statutory limit.
